To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the chemistry of the living plant is different from that of the dead plant.
the headspace vola-tiles over living flowers, fruits, and spices are qualitatively and quantitatively different from the volatiles over the picked plant parts.
the aroma profiles of living and picked plant parts are distinctly different and that the differences in the volatile profiles are caused by the biological death of the plant part.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the chemistry of living plants and the chemistry of their products, i.e., the chemistry of living vs. dead plant parts.
the chemistry and biochemistry of volatile flavor and fragrance compounds.

the development of a new technology that permits a better understanding of the chemistry of flowers, fruit, herbs, and spice aromas and that can be used to better control the quality of these products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the living flowers, fruits, and spices are the true source of their characteristic aromas.
the aroma of the plant part changes after the plant part is picked.
the volatile profiles of the same flowers, fruits, and spices are different when living vs. dead.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the aroma of flowers, fruits, and spices is not a static phenomenon but is a dynamic one.
the chemistry of living vs. dead plant parts is a new dimension in the field of aroma research.
the chemistry of flowers, fruit and spices is not a static science, but rather a dynamic science.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the volatile aroma of flowers, fruits, spices and herbs can be used to distinguish between living and dead plant parts.

the aroma profiles of fruits, flowers and spices are significantly influenced by their biological activity and that the volatile profiles of the same species change significantly over the course of the day.
the aroma profiles of living vs. dead plants are significantly different and that these changes are not only quantitative but also qualitative.
